title: Ring distributive and associative laws
statement: Addition commutes, multiplication associates, and both distributive laws hold.
hypotheses: R is a non-unital ring.
fidelity_note: Four displayed laws; the other additive group axioms remain encoded in the typeclass.

title: Zero-product criterion
statement: a*b=0 iff a=0 or b=0.
hypotheses: R is a commutative domain.
fidelity_note: Covers part 3 of the definition.

title: Wedderburn little theorem
statement: Every finite division ring is a field.
hypotheses: D is a finite division ring.
fidelity_note: Uses Mathlib's finite division-ring field instance.

title: Prime characteristic of a domain
statement: A nontrivial ring without zero divisors has prime characteristic when its characteristic is positive.
hypotheses: R is a nontrivial ring without zero divisors; CharP R p; p is nonzero.
fidelity_note: Nontriviality and positive characteristic are explicit.

title: Finite-field characteristic
statement: The characteristic of a finite field is prime.
hypotheses: K is a finite field.
fidelity_note: The typeclass supplies positive finite-field characteristic.

title: Frobenius preserves addition
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring of prime characteristic p; n is a natural number.
fidelity_note: Prime characteristic is explicit; n=0 is included. The characteristic-four counterexample records why the prime assumption matters.

title: Frobenius preserves finite sums
statement: Raising a finite sum to p^n equals the sum of the p^n powers.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring of prime characteristic p; finite index set; n natural.
fidelity_note: Covers the book's arbitrary finite sum; n=0 and the empty sum are also valid.

title: Cardinality from extension degree
hypotheses: K and L are finite fields with an algebra structure K→L.
fidelity_note: The algebra structure gives the vector-space structure; dimensions are Mathlib finrank.

title: Finite-field prime-power order
statement: A finite field has cardinality p^n for prime p and positive n.
hypotheses: K is finite field of characteristic p.
fidelity_note: Prime-power existence; the dimension identification is in cardinality_prime_field_dimension.

title: Finite-field Fermat rule
statement: a^(|K|-1)=1 for nonzero a.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; a≠0.
fidelity_note: Nonzero-element clause; power_card covers the all-elements clause.

title: Every element satisfies x^q=x
hypotheses: K is a finite field; a is any element.
fidelity_note: All-elements clause including zero.

title: Iterated q-power identity
hypotheses: K is a finite field; n is natural.
fidelity_note: Derived iteration of the all-elements clause.

title: Inverse by exponentiation
hypotheses: K is a finite field; a≠0.
fidelity_note: Includes the two-element field; natural subtraction is justified by |K|≥2.

title: Sum of field elements
statement: The sum of all elements is zero when |K|>2.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; |K|>2.
fidelity_note: Covers the zero-sum assertion; the exceptional field's sum is not a separate declaration.

title: Polynomial q-power expansion
statement: Expanding exponents by q equals raising the polynomial to q.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; f is in K[X]; q=|K|.
fidelity_note: Mathlib expand sends X to X^q, matching the book's notation.

title: Roots of X^q-X
statement: The roots multiset of X^q-X is exactly the multiset of all field elements.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; q=|K|.
fidelity_note: Root multiset statement; field_polynomial_factorization separately proves the displayed product identity.

title: Field polynomial splits
statement: X^|K|-X splits over K.
hypotheses: K is a finite field.
fidelity_note: Only the splitting assertion; existence and uniqueness have separate entries.

title: Cyclic multiplicative group
statement: The nonzero elements of a finite field form a cyclic group.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; nonzero elements are represented as units.
fidelity_note: Uses Mathlib's actual units group.

title: Order of the multiplicative group
hypotheses: K is a finite field.
fidelity_note: Structural ingredient in the primitive-element definition; does not count primitive elements.

title: Polynomial representation of functions
statement: Every function K→K is evaluation of a polynomial.
hypotheses: K is a finite field.
fidelity_note: Existence alone; polynomial_function_bounded supplies the degree bound.

title: Bounded polynomial representation
statement: Every function K→K has a polynomial representative of degree <|K|.
hypotheses: K is a finite field.
fidelity_note: Uses actual Lagrange interpolation; paired with uniqueness this covers the theorem.

title: Uniqueness of bounded representation
statement: Polynomials of degree <|K| agreeing on K are equal.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; both polynomial degrees are <|K|.
fidelity_note: The strict degree hypotheses are necessary.

title: Irreducible degree divisibility test
statement: f divides X^(q^m)-X iff degree(f) divides m.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; f is irreducible; m is natural; q=|K|.
fidelity_note: Includes m=0, where the right polynomial is zero.

title: Permutation criterion on a finite field
statement: A self-map of a finite field is bijective iff it is injective.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; f is a self-map.
fidelity_note: Function-level equivalent criterion; polynomial evaluation is a special case.

title: Irreducible minimal polynomial
statement: The minimal polynomial of an algebraic element is irreducible.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension; a is integral over K (equivalent to algebraic over a field).
fidelity_note: Exposes algebraicity needed for a nonzero minimal polynomial.

title: Tower law
hypotheses: K→L→E is a compatible tower of finite-dimensional field extensions.
fidelity_note: The IsScalarTower hypothesis records map compatibility.

title: Finite extensions are algebraic
statement: Every element of a finite-dimensional field extension is algebraic.
hypotheses: K→L is a finite-dimensional field extension.
fidelity_note: IsIntegral agrees with algebraic over fields.

title: Trace as Frobenius sum
statement: The image of Tr(L/K)(a) in L is the sum of a^(|K|^i) over 0≤i<[L:K].
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Proves the bridge from the book's sum to the standard algebraic trace.

title: Trace is additive
statement: Tr(a+b)=Tr(a)+Tr(b).
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension.
fidelity_note: Part 2. The trace map is a Mathlib linear map.

title: Trace respects base scalars
statement: Tr(c*a)=c*Tr(a).
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension; c lies in K.
fidelity_note: Part 3. Scalar multiplication uses the given algebra map.

title: Trace is onto
statement: Every base-field value is the trace of some extension-field element.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Surjectivity in part 4; separability is inferred from finite fields.

title: Trace of a base element
statement: Tr(algebraMap(a))=[L:K]*a.
hypotheses: K→L is a finite-dimensional field extension; a lies in K.
fidelity_note: Part 5. The extension degree is cast into K.

title: Trace transitivity
statement: Tr(L/K)(Tr(E/L)(a))=Tr(E/K)(a).
hypotheses: K→L→E is a compatible tower of finite-dimensional field extensions.
fidelity_note: Part 8, in composition order.

title: Nondegenerate trace pairing
statement: If a≠0 there exists b with Tr(a*b)≠0.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Proves nondegeneracy; the classification of all linear functionals is still a separate obligation.

title: Norm as Frobenius product
statement: The image of N(L/K)(a) is the product of a^(|K|^i) over 0≤i<[L:K].
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Bridge to the product in the book's definition.

title: Norm by exponentiation
statement: The image of N(L/K)(a) is a^((|L|-1)/(|K|-1)).
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Matches the quotient exponent formula, including zero.

title: Norm is multiplicative
statement: N(a*b)=N(a)*N(b).
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension.
fidelity_note: Part 2, from the standard norm monoid homomorphism.

title: Norm is onto
statement: Every base-field element is a norm.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Part 3 on the full fields, including zero.

title: Norm is onto on nonzero elements
statement: Every nonzero base-field element is the norm of a nonzero extension-field element.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Part 3 restricted to the actual units groups.

title: Norm of a base element
statement: N(algebraMap(a))=a^[L:K].
hypotheses: K→L is a finite-dimensional field extension; a lies in K.
fidelity_note: Part 4.

title: Norm transitivity
hypotheses: K→L→E is a compatible tower of finite-dimensional field extensions.
fidelity_note: Part 6, in composition order.

title: Independent Galois orbit
statement: Some element's Galois orbit is linearly independent over the base field.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Normal-basis ingredient only; primitive normality is not established here.

title: Normal basis theorem
statement: There is a spanning basis consisting of the Galois orbit of one element.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Full normal-basis existence; the additional primitive-element requirement in this remark remains open.

title: Order of Frobenius
statement: The q-power automorphism has order [L:K].
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite; K has a finite enumeration; q=|K|.
fidelity_note: Establishes generator order; frobenius_enumerates gives exhaustive enumeration.

title: Finite-field Galois group is cyclic
statement: The automorphism group of L over K is cyclic.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite.
fidelity_note: Uses the extension field L as required by the editors' erratum.

title: Frobenius powers enumerate automorphisms
statement: The powers indexed by 0≤i<[L:K] biject onto all K-automorphisms of L.
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite; K has a finite enumeration.
fidelity_note: Bijection records distinctness and exhaustiveness.

title: Trace is Frobenius invariant
statement: Tr(a^|K|)=Tr(a).
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite; K has a finite enumeration.
fidelity_note: Part 6, via invariance under K-algebra automorphisms.

title: Norm is Frobenius invariant
hypotheses: K→L is a field extension with L finite; K has a finite enumeration.
fidelity_note: Part 5, via invariance under K-algebra automorphisms.

title: Linearized polynomials preserve addition
statement: Any finite sum of c_i*x^(q^i) preserves addition.
hypotheses: K→L is a finite-field extension; coefficients c_i lie in L; q=|K|.
fidelity_note: Part 1; the proof explicitly bridges Frobenius iterates to polynomial exponents.

title: Linearized polynomials respect base scalars
statement: Any finite sum of c_i*x^(q^i) commutes with multiplication by a base-field scalar.
hypotheses: K→L is a finite-field extension; coefficients c_i lie in L; scalar lies in K.
fidelity_note: Part 2; the same explicit exponent bridge is proved.

title: Finite field of prescribed order
statement: GaloisField(p,n) has cardinality p^n.
hypotheses: p is prime; n is a nonzero natural number.
fidelity_note: The actual GaloisField construction supplies a Field instance. Uniqueness is a separate obligation.

title: Cardinality and prime-field dimension
hypotheses: K is a finite field of prime characteristic p, with its prime-field algebra structure.
fidelity_note: Dimension clause paired with prime-power existence.

title: Euler totient multiplicativity
statement: φ(m*n)=φ(m)*φ(n) when m and n are coprime.
hypotheses: m,n natural; gcd(m,n)=1.
fidelity_note: Includes zero whenever the coprimality premise allows it.

title: Order of a power
statement: ord(g^t)=ord(g)/gcd(ord(g),t).
hypotheses: G is a finite group; g lies in G; t natural.
fidelity_note: The element-order formula underlying the primitive-power criterion; the iff for primitive generators is not separately declared.

title: Irreducible polynomial splits in its degree extension
statement: An irreducible degree-n polynomial over K splits in the degree-n finite-field extension.
hypotheses: K finite field of prime characteristic p; n>0; f irreducible with natDegree f=n.
fidelity_note: Applies the editors' missing irreducibility hypothesis. This proves the first sentence; the following roots-of-unity discussion is not included.

title: Embedding criterion for finite extensions
statement: A K-field embeds into an L-field over F iff its degree over F divides the degree of L over F.
hypotheses: F,K,L finite fields with F-algebra structures on K and L.
fidelity_note: Existence of an embedding; uniqueness of the subfield inside L is not separately declared.

title: Characteristic-four counterexample
statement: (1+1)^4 differs from 1^4+1^4 in Z/4Z.
hypotheses: Arithmetic is in ZMod 4.
fidelity_note: Kernel-reduced counterexample to extending the formula to arbitrary composite characteristic. This clarifies the prime-p convention, rather than alleging an editors-listed erratum.

title: Factorization of X^q-X
statement: X^q-X is the product of X-a over all a in the field.
hypotheses: K is a finite field; q=|K|.
fidelity_note: Exact displayed identity, using monicity and the checked roots multiset.
